overview: Tintagel is a wonderfully dramatic spot: castle ruins scattered across a headland and a rocky island on the north coast, a short walk down from Tintagel village. Long before the castle, between the 5th and 7th centuries, this was an important settlement of Cornish rulers who traded as far afield as the Mediterranean. Richard, Earl of Cornwall built the castle you see the remains of in the 13th century.

The legend is what gets most people here. Writing in the 12th century, Geoffrey of Monmouth claimed King Arthur was conceived at Tintagel, and English Heritage, who look after the site, lean into the story with sculpture and displays. Even if you’re not into Arthur, the wild, windswept setting on the cliffs is worth the trip on its own.
It’s all outdoors on steep, exposed ground with plenty of steps, so pick a dry day and wear proper shoes.

expect.title: The footbridge
expect.text: A modern footbridge spans the gap between the mainland and the island, roughly where the medieval castle’s two halves were once joined. You cross at the time on your ticket, then explore the island at your own pace.

expect.title: Ruins and early settlement
expect.text: On the island you’ll find the remains of the 13th-century Great Hall and outlines of much older houses, with outdoor panels explaining what you’re looking at.

expect.title: Gallos
expect.text: A life-sized bronze figure inspired by the Arthur legend looks out to sea from the island. It’s the photo everyone takes.

expect.title: Beach and Merlin’s Cave
expect.text: At low tide a small sandy beach appears below the castle, with a big sea cave known as Merlin’s Cave to explore.

expect.title: Exhibition and café
expect.text: By the entrance there’s an exhibition on the history and legends, a shop and a café with sea views.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Entry is paid and free for English Heritage members. Booking online by midnight the day before saves money, and tickets are valid all day.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: There’s no car park at the castle. Use one of the paid car parks in the village, about 600 metres away, and give yourself a good half hour to walk down before your bridge time.

goodToKnow.label: The walk down
goodToKnow.text: The path to the site is steep. A limited shuttle runs from near the shop and café, but you still walk the last stretch.

goodToKnow.label: Weather
goodToKnow.text: The castle sometimes shuts in high winds, so check the English Heritage website or social media before setting off if it’s stormy.

goodToKnow.label: Toilets
goodToKnow.text: There are toilets by the shop and café at the bottom of Castle Road, plus public ones in the village.

week.text: Tintagel makes a great half-day on a dry day in north Cornwall, and fits well with a lazy afternoon on a beach nearby. Check the tide times if you want to see Merlin’s Cave and the beach below the castle.

pairWith.why: a sandy surf beach, at its biggest around low tide
a quieter cove a short drive up the coast
a pretty harbour village a few miles along the coast

tips: Book a bridge slot early in the day in summer and you’ll have more space on the island.
Leave pushchairs in the car: there are lots of steps.
Time your visit with low tide if you want to explore the beach and Merlin’s Cave.
